key_insight: MedCheckpoint combines LLM agents with fixed study designs, deterministic statistical tools, and feasibility checkpoints to improve automated drug-safety research reliability.
clinical_relevance: The system could support more auditable postmarketing drug-safety analyses, but its performance in real clinical datasets remains unproven.
method: Ground analytical stages in curated, source-traceable medical knowledge.
Lock core study-design parameters and use human-written deterministic tools for patient-level analyses.
Abort infeasible analyses through checkpoints, with optional human review.
evidence_signal: On 54 questions using simulated EHRs for 2.7 million individuals, MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines on LLM-rated report quality and consistency, with no misleading failures across seven stress-test trap questions.
watch_item: Simulated data and LLM-judged report quality do not establish real-world drug-safety detection performance.
paper_title: Automating postmarketing pharmacovigilance with large language model agents
